As shown in Figure 24a, a substantial improvement in the lifetime of PCSs is observed with the IZO/TCC encapsulation, maintaining above 90% of their initial PCEs for up to 1,430 hours. In comparison, the unencapsulated control sample measured 88% of its initial efficiency after 336 hours, which progressively declined to 64% of its initial PCE at the 1,430-hour mark. Interpolating the efficiency between measurements (T95 at 168hrs., and T88 at 336hrs.) shows that the unencapsulated PSC reaches 90% of its initial PCE after approx. 288 hours. This corresponds to a near 5-fold improvement in the stabilities of the encapsulated PSCs with a single IZO/TCC dyad. The PV performances of the champion encapsulated PSC and the control sample before (0 hr.) and after 1,430 hours of aging are summarized in Figure 24b (illumination from glass/ITO), Figure 24c (illumination through IZO/TCC) and Table 13. These figures clearly illustrate the improved stability provided by the IZO/TCC encapsulation.
